name: experienceOS
tagline: One platform for experiential agencies to run campaigns, staffing, assets, live capture, and client reporting.
description: experienceOS is a full-stack platform for experiential marketing agencies and live event teams. I built the product across the marketing site and the operating system itself: campaign setup, event scheduling, staffing, asset tracking, field execution, dashboards, and reporting, so a program no longer lives in spreadsheets.

problem: Agencies running live activations keep campaigns, staff schedules, assets, lead capture, and client reports in different spreadsheets and chats. Nothing stays in sync once the event starts, and the recap is rebuilt by hand afterwards.
approach: Treat the campaign as the system of record. Set the program up once — events, locations, roles, and assets — then run staffing, field capture, and reporting against that same campaign instead of starting a new document for each activation.
solution: A connected platform agencies use from planning through the recap. Teams define the campaign framework, assign staff and vendors, capture engagement while the activation is live, and pull dashboards and client-ready reports from the same data. The public site explains the product, who it is for, and how a team gets from setup to reports.
features: Campaign framework with events, locations, roles, and reusable program structure
Event scheduling and asset allocation across activations
Staff assignments, vendor details, custom forms, and task workflows
Live execution: engagement capture, issue logging, and team coordination
Dashboards, auto-generated reports, and export for clients
Templates and past-campaign data so the next activation starts from what already worked
Separate paths for agencies and event companies, including a public marketing site
architecture: A full-stack web application: a public marketing site plus an authenticated operations product. Campaign, staffing, asset, and reporting workflows share one data model so field activity and client reports read from the same records.
